content:
Elaine (Sales): Hey team — Acme Health is kicking off a 2-week POC next Monday and asked if we can temporarily raise hosted API throughput. They want ~250 req/s for text-gen peaks and about 40-60 concurrent streaming sessions. Is a hosted quota bump feasible or will this need Dedicated?
Sam (SE): can you drop the project/org id, model they plan to use, and exact timeframe? also what latency SLA do they expect?
Elaine (Sales): Org: acme-health-poc. Model: redwood-2-medium (mostly single-turn + streaming). POC window: 2024-06-03 -> 2024-06-17. Latency: <400ms median, spikes ok up to 1s. They have credits but want predictable perf.
Devon (Infra): short answer: yes, we can do a hosted quota increase for a short POC, but it needs an infra approval and capacity check. Default per-key and per-org limits are conservative for multi-tenant safety. For this scale we usually do a temporary override with an expiry and monitoring hooks.
Devon (Infra): Required info we need in the request:
```
- org_id: acme-health-poc
- contact (email + phone): (Elaine or Rachel)
- peak req/s and sustained req/s: peak 250 rps, sustained ~150 rps
- concurrency for streaming: 50 concurrent sessions
- model + avg tokens per request: redwood-2-medium, ~400 tokens/request
- start_ts and end_ts: 2024-06-03 -> 2024-06-17
- reason: timeboxed POC to validate latency/cost
```
Devon (Infra): once we get that, we run a capacity check and if green we create a quota override with an automatic expiration and alerting. Typical turnaround is 24-48 hrs (can be faster if low-impact).
Elaine (Sales): thanks. I’ll file the request. who signs off on cost/billing if they exceed free credits?
Rachel (AM): Account side — if they exceed free credits during the POC we notify customer and ask them to approve pay-as-you-go charges; we can also cap spend. Elaine, pls confirm if they want an enforced spend cap.
Elaine (Sales): they want to start without hard cap but get alerts at 50%, 80%, 100%.
Sam (SE): For monitoring, enable per-route metrics in Console and add a short eval set to catch quality regressions during scale. I’ll set up dashboards: latency, 5xx rate, tokens/sec.
Devon (Infra): here’s a minimal internal ticket payload you can paste into the infra queue:
```json
{
  "type":"quota_increase_request",
  "org":"acme-health-poc",
  "contact":"elaine@redwood.com",
  "peak_rps":250,
  "sustained_rps":150,
  "concurrent_streams":50,
  "model":"redwood-2-medium",
  "avg_tokens_per_request":400,
  "start":"2024-06-03T00:00:00Z",
  "end":"2024-06-17T23:59:00Z",
  "notes":"POC for Acme Health. Requesting temporary hosted quota bump. Please add auto-expire and alerting."
}
```
Devon (Infra): after submit, ping me here and I’ll prioritize the capacity check. Also add whether they need cross-region failover (us-east + eu-west) — that changes capacity planning.
Elaine (Sales): no cross-region for this POC, single region us-east. Submitting now.
quota-bot: Ticket #INFRA-4821 created by Elaine (Sales) — status: triage. Link: https://internal.jira/INFRA-4821
Devon (Infra): got it, I’ll run the load simulation against staging nodes and confirm. Expect an update in ~6-12 hrs.
Sam (SE): once override is in place I’ll route a small canary traffic set and verify KV cache and batching behave under the higher qps. I’ll also enable streaming health checks.
Rachel (AM): I’ll draft the customer note with alert thresholds and billing note. Elaine — can you confirm the POC contact info in the ticket?
Elaine (Sales): confirmed. Thanks — will update if Acme wants a hard spend cap.
Devon (Infra): quick note: if we see sustained >200 rps with long token lengths, we may recommend a short Dedicated trial since tail latency and cost predictability become better. But for a 2-week POC hosted override should be fine.
Sam (SE): FYI — please add these console alerts:
- tokens/sec > expected * 1.5
- 5xx rate > 0.5%
- median latency > 500ms
Devon (Infra): override will include configurable throttles and auto-fallback to a lower-rate policy if errors spike.
Elaine (Sales): awesome. I’ll update Acme and share the ticket link. cc @Rachel (AM) @Sam (SE)
Rachel (AM): thanks — I’ll follow up with onboarding notes and billing expectations.
